title: E2 — Mutation engine — 6 ops, 4 invariants, CAS
description:
The code that stands between the LLM and the file. Builds a candidate graph in memory, checks the invariants, and only then touches disk — so a bad batch is never half-applied.

Cut from 11 ops and 9 invariants by the §0.5 simplification pass. T2.6 is never-cut.

spec.md §6.4, §6.7 · 11h human / 2.8h AI

title: T2.1 — The 6 ops — apply functions, fixed internal order
description:
add_node · add_edge · set_status · record_outcome · record_output · supersede_node.

Internal order: additions and rewires BEFORE cancellations (Zeebe). A batch violating that order is rejected, never silently reordered.

**§0.5 deleted five ops** — `fan_out`, `add_wait`, `insert_compensation`, `reroute_edge`, `resolve_gate`. All five were `add_node`/`add_edge` with sugar: **the atomic unit is the commit, not the op**, so a batch already gives the all-or-nothing guarantee `fan_out` existed to provide. That also deletes the auto-wiring table (old T2.3), which caused every orphan in the v2 probe.

No `delete_node`. No `rollback` opcode, not even reserved.

---
**Effort:** 2.5h / 40m · **Epic:** E2 · **Spec:** docs/spec.md · **Plan:** docs/plan.md T2.1

title: T2.2 — Symbolic intra-batch references ($0, $2.children.dana)

title: T2.4 — The 4 enforced invariants + parser + CAS check
description:
**A zod parser first, free:** schema validity (legal type + required fields; legal edge kind; a `condition` on every gate/wait out-edge) and every wait/gate having a deadline + `on_timeout`. Those are *shape*, not graph properties — they were invariants 1 and 4 until §0.5.

**Then four invariants:**
1 terminal & effect protection — an **op-delta** predicate against pre-commit head state
2 quorum stays satisfiable
3 effect budget (the circuit breaker that replaced human gates)
4 **recipients must be evidenced** — the highest-value check in the codebase; it is what stops the mutator inventing people to email

Plus CAS on `parent_v`.

**#1 is an op-delta predicate, not a post-state scan** — as a state predicate it rejected every commit once any node reached `done`.

Stryker target: 100.

---
**Effort:** 2h / 30m · **Epic:** E2 · **Spec:** docs/spec.md · **Plan:** docs/plan.md T2.4

title: T2.6 — Branch resolution — store drops untaken branches
description:
**NEVER CUT.** On terminal resolution the store marks untaken branch targets `dropped`, transitively, stopping at any node still held by a live blocking in-edge. An in-edge whose SOURCE is dropped is excluded from merge evaluation.

Readiness fails safe and does NOT inherit the exclusion — otherwise the second node on an untaken branch has no blocker, lands on the frontier, and gets dispatched.

Without this, v2's dominant silent deadlock returns.

---
**Effort:** 3h / 45m · **Epic:** E2 · **Spec:** docs/spec.md · **Plan:** docs/plan.md T2.6

title: T2.7 — flock + compare-and-swap on parent_v
description:
Exit 3 + `STALE_BASE_VERSION` + current head on mismatch. Re-read and re-decide, never blind-merge.

Beads #5898: 54 cross-actor overwrites, median 31 min apart — the enemy is hand-offs, not races.

title: T3.3 — Outbox — reserve, fsync, send, record
description:
`effect_key = hash(node_id, created_by_version)` — **payload-independent by design**. `payload_hash` computed at reserve. Same key + different payload_hash = loud error, never a second send.

title: T4.1 — Verb scaffolding, --json, exit codes
description:
Exit status is 8-bit: **0** ok · **1** refused · **3** stale base version · **4** invariant violation. `409` would truncate to `153`.

Every non-zero exit writes one stderr line beginning with a symbolic reason code — `STALE_BASE_VERSION` (+ head), `INVARIANT_VIOLATION` (+ invariant and node), `REFUSED` (+ reason).

(Code 5 `NODE_LEASED` was removed by §0.5 — with one writer there is nothing to lease.)

title: T4.2 — `kona brief` — subgraph + identity, correlation, preconditions
description:
The v1 probe found 0/8 fresh subagents could execute; the v2 fix added nine blocks and got 10/10. **§0.5 observes six of the nine were derivable all along** — once `outputs` is declared and `record_output` fills it, resolved inputs, status, gate decisions, recipient, time and the ledger are a walk over the folded graph.

**Three genuinely are not in the graph:**
- `identity` — sending mailbox, display name, signature, **and an authority statement**
- `correlation` — the **fully-expanded literal** reply-to and subject tag (one trial emitted `kona+…@<kona-inbox>` verbatim)
- `preconditions_satisfied` — computed by the CLI and **fails CLOSED**; in v2 it read true while an input was UNRESOLVED

Plus `disclosable`. Returns all of it or refuses.
